contents.text: Ancient Egyptian civilization started along the Nile River. Other ancient civilizations also started near rivers. For example, ancient Mesopotamian civilizations started along the Tigris and Euphrates Rivers, ancient Indus Valley civilizations started along the Indus River, and ancient Chinese civilization began between the Yellow and Yangtze Rivers.

explanationText.text: Horus is the god of Egyptian kings. He is often shown with the head of a falcon and the body of a man. He is considered to be the son of the god Osiris.

Sekhmet is the goddess of war. She is often shown with the face of a lion and wearing a sun disc on her head. Ancient Egyptian kings would sometimes say that Sekhmet rode with them into battle to destroy enemies. She was sometimes called "she who dances on blood."

text.text: Around 2500 BCE, kings living in Lower Egypt controlled most of the Egyptian land.
<atomic>Two popular sun gods in Lower Egypt were Atum and Ra.</atomic>
<atomic>Ra represented the midday sun and Atum represented the setting sun.</atomic>
<atomic>Sometimes, to represent the whole sun, Ra and Atum were combined into one god, Atum-Ra.</atomic>
<atomic>In contrast, in Upper Egypt the popular sun god was Amun.</atomic>
By 1500 BCE, kings living in Upper Egypt gained power over both Upper and Lower Egypt.
<atomic>As a result, Amun and Ra were combined to become Amun-Ra.</atomic>

header.text: In most ancient Egyptian religious traditions, two or more gods could combine to form a single god. Read the passage. Then follow the instructions below.

pieces.text: Around 2500 BCE, kings in

controlled most of the Egyptian land. Two popular sun gods in Lower Egypt were Atum and Ra. Ra represented the midday sun and Atum represented the setting sun. Sometimes, to represent the whole sun, Ra and Atum were combined into one god, Atum-Ra.
In contrast, in Upper Egypt the popular sun god was Amun. By 1500 BCE, kings in
gained power over both Upper and Lower Egypt. As a result, Amun and Ra were combined to become Amun-Ra.

. At that time, Kush did not have its own written language. So today, researchers study objects and buildings instead of written sources to learn about the Kerman Kingdom. Read the description of the largest monument in the Kerman Kingdom. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: The Western Deffufa (duh-FOO-fuh) is one of the oldest monuments in Africa. It was built by the rulers of the Kerman Kingdom around 2000 BCE. When the Western Deffufa was built, it was one of the largest buildings in the region. Today, even though some of the building has crumbled away, it is still around 60 feet tall. That's about as tall as a six-story building!
Because the Western Deffufa was so large, it took many workers to build it. The rulers of the Kerman Kingdom used their powerful armies and wealth to force workers to build the Western Deffufa.

The Western Deffufa was made out of a common building material called mudbrick. Each brick had to be individually shaped and then baked in the sun. Then people needed to transport the bricks to the construction site and stack them up to make the walls of the building. This process took a lot of time. It also cost the Kerman rulers a lot of money to feed all of the workers.

. At that time, Kush did not have its own written language. So today, researchers study objects and buildings instead of written sources to learn about the Kerman Kingdom. Read the description of the largest monument in the Kerman Kingdom. Then answer the question below.

textContent.text: The Western Deffufa (duh-FOO-fuh) is one of the oldest monuments in Africa. It was built by the rulers of the Kerman Kingdom around 2000 BCE. When the Western Deffufa was built, it was one of the largest buildings in the region. Today, even though some of the building has crumbled away, it is still around 60 feet tall. That's about as tall as a six-story building!
Because the Western Deffufa was so large, it took many workers to build it. The rulers of the Kerman Kingdom used their powerful armies and wealth to force workers to build the Western Deffufa.

The Western Deffufa was made out of a common building material called mudbrick. Each brick had to be individually shaped and then baked in the sun. Then people needed to transport the bricks to the construction site and stack them up to make the walls of the building. This process took a lot of time. It also cost the Kerman rulers a lot of money to feed all of the workers.

textContent.text: The first Zhou king conquered a large amount of territory. In order to rule such a large territory, the king gave pieces of land to his lords. Lords controlled their local regions, but they still paid taxes and pledged allegiance to the Zhou king. As long as the lords served the Zhou king, they were allowed to keep this land. This period of the Zhou Dynasty, known as the early Zhou period, lasted from 1046 to 771 BCE.

pieces.text: After several hundred years, Zhou lords became so powerful that they no longer wanted to serve the king. Lords began to claim land for themselves and fight other lords for land and for power. Historians call this time the period of Warring States. During the Warring States period, some lords
, or took over, other lords' land. These lords became the rulers of large states.

content.text: If people had individual ambitions, they may not want to fight in wars.

explanationText.text: Wars are dangerous and require people to make sacrifices. Having personal ambitions might make a person reject the government's goal of promoting war.

content.text: Wanting to live a long life could prevent soldiers from fighting in wars.

explanationText.text: Fighting wars was often dangerous. Wanting to live a long life could make people not want to fight in wars.

content.text: Beauty and love could distract people from working hard.

explanationText.text: Shang Yang wanted nearly all men to engage in agriculture or war. Appreciating beauty and wanting love could distract them from this work.

content.text: If a soldier loved his parents, he would fight more bravely.

explanationText.text: Shang Yang believed that love was a parasite, meaning that it had a negative effect on society. So, Shang Yang would not have agreed with the idea that a person who loved his parents would be a braver soldier.

content.text: If neighbors reported crimes to the government right away, they would usually not be punished for their neighbors' crimes. But if people failed to report their neighbor's crime, they would be punished harshly

content.text: These laws kept people from committing crimes.

explanationText.text: Qin laws encouraged people to monitor their neighbors and forced people to report their neighbors' crimes to the government. If neighbors didn't report these crimes, they could be punished. So, people knew their neighbors would report them and were therefore less likely to commit crimes.

header.text: Building cities such as Chang'an in the Han Empire required thousands of workers. Read the passage about the construction of Han cities. Then follow the instructions below.

textContent.text: Thousands of workers were needed for large projects such as building cities or canals. The Han government required people in their territory to work for at least 30 days a year on these projects.

One important project was a new city wall. Between 194 and 190 BCE, the first Han emperor ordered workers to build a large wall around the new capital city. The wall was almost 40 feet high, over 50 feet thick, and almost 16 miles long. That's about as tall as a house with 4 floors!

pieces.text: Different groups of people played different roles in these projects. People who had committed crimes were forced to do physical labor. Other people helped with planning and decoration. For example,
, or people who design buildings, were in charge of planning the layout of cities. Craftsmen decorated the city walls and the doors and roofs of Han buildings.
